clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-203], sentence 2: "With all five candle flames lit and a tear delay of 2, an active vulnerable enemy standing next to the player can remain completely undamaged."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:503-544 lights the five candles through their GetData().IsLit/LitTimer fields, forces MaxFireDelay=2 every frame and requires at least one MC_ENTITY_TAKE_DMG hit and HP < 99 within 8 frames.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-203], sentence 3: "At a tear delay of 4 ... the aura pulses every frame, roughly twice as often as the intended rounded interval."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:545-549 requires exactly 4 damage callbacks in an 8-frame window at MaxFireDelay=4 (the unchanged starter produces 8). The intended interval of 2 frames is only implied publicly by "roughly twice as often".

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-217]: "A wounded player with six red-heart containers and two filled hearts is left with one filled heart, while the conversion should empty the red hearts consistently for that capacity."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:994-1002 checks the single reported data point (max=12, red=4 -> red=0, max still 12). It does not probe a second fill level, so capacity-based and empty-everything readings both pass.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-281]: "each copy keeps the original current health while its maximum is halved, leaving current health above the displayed maximum"
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:705-759 retries up to 16 rounds of eight killed Horfs and requires >= 2 shrunken copies, none with HitPoints > MaxHitPoints + 0.01.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-303]: "Each later use is meant to add a smaller, diminishing stat increase rather than no increase at all."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:315-358. tragic_mushroom_repeat requires the second use to raise damage, speed and range by > 0.05; tragic_mushroom_diminishing requires the third gain to be > 0.05 and smaller than the second for all three stats. See known_issues[1] for the speed cap.

known_issues: Fixture trap: tragic_mushroom_diminishing (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:343-351) requires the third speed gain to be > 0.05 while the engine clamps MoveSpeed at 2.0. Isaac starts at 1.0 and the first use adds 0.6, so only 0.4 of headroom is left for uses two and three; any valid diminishing series whose second speed gain is >= 0.35 (decay ratio >= ~0.58) reports a third gain <= 0.05 and fails. The reference itself only shows 0.10 instead of its nominal 0.15.

ritual_candle_cadence (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:548) requires exactly 4 damage callbacks in 8 frames. The 2-frame interval is only implied publicly ("roughly twice as often as the intended rounded interval"); nearest-integer rounding of 4/3 gives 1 and keeps 8 hits, so only a ceil-like reading passes.

Order dependence: the thirty main-suite cases share one run and one player (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:264-1009). State leaks forward (Forbidden Fruit's +0.99 damage is part of every later damage figure; Mutant Clover is silently replaced by Anamnesis before its reset guard; a pcall failure in any step emits GCB_FATAL and leaves every later case unobserved).

Shared game-log markers (private NOTES.md, Verifier design): results are parsed from unauthenticated `[GCB_CASE]` lines written through Isaac.DebugString into the same log the submission can write to, so outcomes are only meaningful under the honest-code assumption.

Process coupling: the secret-room process runs with continued=true as player_type=18 (James), inheriting the James process's run from Steam's in-memory cache (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/test.sh:85-108). apocryphon_stats and blue_moon are therefore measured on James, who already owns The Apocryphon.

validation/case-contracts.tsv labels eight cases `guard`; two of them (tragic_mushroom_diminishing, anamnesis_charge_persistence) fail in the unchanged starter and are mapped as target here. validation/predicate-matrix.tsv agrees: the EX-303 and EX-318 single-report candidates newly pass them.

Launch harness: this task runs the frozen composite's three suites and test.sh unchanged, but the Hub mounts the task's own tests/run-game.sh over the image's copy. That script queues the launch request as soon as the offline Steam client proper is up, repeats an ignored request once, replaces a client that takes none (up to four starts per game process), and allows longer wall-clock budgets. It decides no case. The image's launch sequence left game processes unstarted on the congested host on 2026-09-23 (UTC); see NOTES.md.
